title: Why gas stations barely profit from gas (and why they can't quit it)

hook.a: Stations earn about thirteen cents a gallon on gas.
hook.b: The card network takes almost as much as the gas station keeps.

numbers.label: Drivers who think stations make $2+/gal
numbers.source: NACS, Who Makes Money Selling Gas? (Jeff Lenard)

numbers.label: Average gross margin on a gallon
numbers.status: verified (trade body). NACS says it used 2020's average; 2025 gross margins averaged over 40¢ (NACS Magazine, June 2026)
numbers.formula: Waterfall starts at 35.7¢ (OPIS weekly average, 2025-01-30); NACS rounds to 35¢. Other costs shown as one bar = 6¢ delivery + 6¢ station + 2¢ equipment + 1¢ shrink = 15¢ (computed from NACS items).

numbers.label: Net margin after costs, NACS example
numbers.value: about 13¢ (its itemised costs add to 23.4¢, leaving 11.6¢)
numbers.status: verified (trade body); an illustration, NACS publishes no 2025 net per gallon; the 13¢ mixes a 2020 gross with 2023 card fees
numbers.formula: Net = 35¢ gross - (6¢ delivery + 8.4¢ card fees + 6¢ store + 2¢ equipment + 1¢ shrink = 23.4¢) = 11.6¢; NACS states ~13¢ (its costs total '22¢'). Card fees / gross = 8.4 / 35.7 = 23.5%. Typical station: 1.5M gal x 11.6-13¢ = $174K-$195K a year before tax.

numbers.label: Typical in-store transaction after ALL expenses
numbers.value: +1¢ in 2024, -7¢ in 2025 (avg basket $7.69); NACS: 'fuel margins were the reason stores were profitable in 2025'
numbers.source: NACS Magazine, 5 Key Metrics Defining the Convenience Industry's Health
numbers.status: verified (trade body; self-reported sample of 35,000+ stores; NACS lobbies on card fees)

analysis.title: Where 35.7 cents a gallon goes, and who pays the bills
analysis.finding: Of a ~35¢ gross margin, card fees take 8.4¢ (23.5%), leaving about 12-13¢ in NACS's example. A typical 1.5M-gallon station illustration is $174K-$195K a year. Inside, the average 2025 trip lost 7¢ after every cost, and NACS says fuel margins are why stores were profitable.

scenes.vo: [flat, confident] Stations earn about thirteen cents
the gross markup near thirty-five cents.
[lowered voice, teasing] So where does it all go?
[excited, sharing a find] Card fees alone take eight point four.
The station's own costs take the rest.
[surprised, building] That leaves about thirteen cents a gallon.
It's NACS's example, and margins ran higher in twenty twenty-five.
[low, a little incredulous] And the store inside?
NACS says the average trip lost seven cents last year, after every cost.
scenes.sub: avg inside trip, after all costs, 2025

scenes.vo: But it's what pays the bills.
[quiet, knowing] That's why stations can't quit the pump.
